text:
Zach Benson's third season has the strangest split on Buffalo's roster. He plays 20:14 a night, up more than four minutes, and the Sabres own the ice when he is out there: 62% of the five-on-five shot attempts and 60% of the expected goals, with a team-best relative mark. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating 0.30 more expected goals per 60 with him on last season, 98th percentile among forwards.

And yet two goals on 6.8 expected. He is shooting 4.8% on 42 shots against a normal range of about 9.5 to 14%. That will turn. The catch is that his assists have been helped by teammates finishing above their chances (Buffalo is 9.1 goals ahead of expected with him on), so the totals may hold steady even as the mix changes, fewer helpers and more goals.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving the zone with possession 64% of the time. Our projection lands him around 20 goals and 71 points. If you are watching one Sabre for a goal binge, it's him.
headline: Benson is driving play, and the puck won't go in
